sources.label: Current cUSD CapToken implementation and Vault source

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Explicit inherited: the verified stcUSD wrapper imposes no direct holder restriction, and its material freeze exposure routes through its ERC-4626 claim on the named upstream cusd-cap, whose verified Vault exposes governance-controlled protocol- and asset-level pause. The wrapper's bounded UUPS upgrade path (external AccessControl, one-day TimelockController, 3-of-5 governance Safe) can introduce a future holder control but none is deployed.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Historical July 30, 2026 review at Ethereum block 25570002 identified StakedCap 0x42c0e0ef7c2f35de073f4d6f9c0e4483429c3d31 and parent CapToken 0xa76645e15c267b876999bf7689e0b2c1ee29bfe6. Rechecked October 1, 2026 at Ethereum block 26095797: stcUSD still resolves to that StakedCap implementation and asset() still returns cUSD 0xcccc62962d17b8914c62d74ffb843d73b2a3cccc; cUSD now resolves to CapToken 0xbdaa34082f1a1a3c32190a672bc9dd1b69791b97. The current verified StakedCap source retains standard ERC-4626 share transfers without a deployed direct blacklist or pause function. The current verified parent Vault retains checkAccess-gated pauseProtocol() and pauseAsset(), so the inherited upstream exposure remains. stcUSD's external AccessControl address remains 0x7731129a10d51e18cde607c5c115f26503d2c683; its default admin remains TimelockController 0xd8236031d8279d82e615af2bfab5fc0127a329ab, whose minimum delay remains 86400 seconds and whose proposer, executor, and canceller roles remain assigned to the 3-of-5 governance Safe. No enabled Safe modules were returned. This current observation covers Ethereum only; newly disclosed MegaETH, Tempo, and Katana stcUSD deployments require separate route and control verification before an exhaustive deployment-scope claim.
